lines.text: Bigger number, bigger shield? On a sunscreen, not the way you'd think.
lines.phonemes: bˈɪɡə nˈʌmbə, bˈɪɡə ʃˈiːld? ˌɒn ɐ sˈʌnskɹiːn, nˌɒt ðə wˈeɪ juːd θˈɪŋk.

lines.text: The number isn't a percentage. It's a ratio: how much more burning light your skin can take under the film before it reddens.
lines.phonemes: ðə nˈʌmbəɹ ˌɪzənt ɐ pəsˈɛntɪdʒ. ɪts ɐ ɹˈeɪʃɪˌəʊ: hˌaʊ mˈʌtʃ mˈɔː bˈɜːnɪŋ lˈaɪt jɔː skˈɪn kan tˈeɪk ˌʌndə ðə fˈɪlm bɪfˌɔːɹ ɪt ɹˈɛdənz.

lines.text: Flip it around, and both let only a thin sliver of that light through, so the bigger number blocks barely more.
lines.phonemes: flˈɪp ɪt ɐɹˈaʊnd, and bˈəʊθ lˈɛt ˈəʊnli ɐ θˈɪn slˈɪvəɹ ɒv ðat lˈaɪt θɹˈuː, sˌəʊ ðə bˈɪɡə nˈʌmbə blˈɒks bˈeəli mˈɔː.

lines.text: But look at what actually gets in. Half as much. That's the real difference, as long as the film is as thick as the lab's.
lines.phonemes: bˌʌt lˈʊk at wɒt ˈaktʃuːəli ɡˈɛts ˈɪn. hˈɑːf az mˈʌtʃ. ðats ðə ɹˈiəl dˈɪfɹəns, az lˈɒŋ az ðə fˈɪlm ɪz az θˈɪk az ðə lˈabz.

lines.text: But real people, studies found, spread a quarter to half as much, and protection falls well below the label. How far is still argued.
lines.phonemes: bˌʌt ɹˈiəl pˈiːpəl, stˈʌdiz fˈaʊnd, spɹˈɛd ɐ kwˈɔːtə tə hˈɑːf az mˈʌtʃ, and pɹətˈɛkʃən fˈɔːlz wˈɛl bɪlˌəʊ ðə lˈeɪbəl. hˌaʊ fˈɑːɹ ɪz stˈɪl ˈɑːɡjuːd.

lines.text: That lab layer is about as thick as the dead layer under it. A fifth of a sheet of paper.
lines.phonemes: ðat lˈab lˈeɪəɹ ɪz ɐbˌaʊt az θˈɪk az ðə dˈɛd lˈeɪəɹ ˈʌndəɹ ɪt. ɐ fˈɪfθ əvə ʃˈiːt ɒv pˈeɪpə.

lines.text: So the bigger number isn't twice the shield. It's half the light getting in, when there's enough of it.
lines.phonemes: sˌəʊ ðə bˈɪɡə nˈʌmbəɹ ˌɪzənt twˈaɪs ðə ʃˈiːld. ɪts hˈɑːf ðə lˈaɪt ɡˌɛtɪŋ ˈɪn, wˌɛn ðeəz ɪnˈʌf ɒv ɪt.

lines.text: Next: why do fingers wrinkle in the bath, but not your arm?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst: wˌaɪ dˈuː fˈɪŋɡəz ɹˈɪŋkəl ɪnðə bˈaθ, bˌʌt nˌɒt jɔːɹ ˈɑːm?
